title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typed fragment, stamped 495 and with a bracketed label 35. It sits between handwritten pages on unrelated topics. The previous page computes p-adic valuations of n! and p^n/n! for divided powers. The next page deals with truncations τ_N and Hom^d in a category of filtered complexes. The fragment is most likely a reused sheet from a long typescript on Dieudonné crystals and the de Rham / Hodge filtration of degenerating abelian varieties. It is not part of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes proper.

Setting, as I reconstruct it:
- There is a sequence of group schemes T → A^♮ → A. Here A^♮ is a semi-abelian 'Raynaud-type' extension, T is its toric part, and A is the degenerating abelian variety (or 1-motive) uniformized by A^♮. This follows SGA 7 IX-style notation.
- 𝓔 = 𝓔(A) is the de Rham / Dieudonné (universal extension) module.
- 𝓔^t ⊂ 𝓔^f ⊂ 𝓔 is the weight (monodromy) filtration: the toric part, then the 'finite' (A^♮) part.
- F̲ ⊂ 𝓔 is the Hodge filtration, with exact sequence (13.4.3): 0 → F̲ → 𝓔 → E̲ = Lie(A) → 0.

Functoriality applied to T → A^♮ → A identifies two things:
- F̲(A^♮) ≅ F̲^f := F̲ ∩ 𝓔^f.
- F̲(T) = F̲^t := F̲ ∩ 𝓔^t, and this is 0.

The vanishing holds because for a torus T the Hodge sequence reads 0 → 0 → 𝓔(T) → Lie(T) → 0: the de Rham module of a torus is entirely 'Lie'. Consequently the composite 𝓔^t → 𝓔 → E̲ is injective, and it induces an isomorphism of 𝓔^t onto Lie(T) ⊂ Lie(A). The page breaks off just before the target of that isomorphism is written.

The mathematical content is the standard compatibility between the Hodge filtration and the weight filtration for a semi-abelian / degenerating abelian scheme: Gr^W_{top} meets the Hodge filtration trivially.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The final statement is truncated: the target of the isomorphism (presumably Lie(T) ⊂ E̲) is not written on this page.
The identification of A^♮ and A (Raynaud extension vs. abelian quotient) is inferred from the notation and is not certain from this page alone.

ideas.what: Hodge filtration of a torus vanishes: 𝓔(T) ≅ Lie(T), F̲(T)=0
ideas.modern_name: Universal vector extension / de Rham realization of a torus (pure of type (-1,-1) / Tate twist)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in Grothendieck's 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974) and SGA 7 IX; unsure about this exact statement

ideas.what: Intersecting the Hodge filtration with the toric/finite weight filtration of the de Rham module of a degenerating abelian variety: F^f = F∩𝓔^f, F^t = F∩𝓔^t = 0, and 𝓔^t ≅ Lie(T)
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of Hodge and weight (monodromy) filtrations for 1-motives / Raynaud extensions; mixed Hodge structure of a 1-motive
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge III, 1974); Raynaud; later Faltings–Chai
ideas.where_published: Closest are SGA 7 exp. IX (filtration by toric/finite parts) and the theory of 1-motives; unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed scrap from a longer typescript, reused in the notes and unrelated to the surrounding handwritten pages. Its content is a routine compatibility of Hodge and weight filtrations for semi-abelian degenerations, well covered by Deligne's 1-motives and later work. The only mild interest is archival: evidence of a ~500-page typescript on this topic. The fragment itself is too short to identify that typescript.
